clue.text: Self-conceit being dispelled, see out engagement

indicators.note: dispelled means scattered, so the letters of the hyphenated phrase are broken up and rearranged
see out tells us the letters S, E, E are taken away from the scattered pool

explanation.surface: Someone's vanity has evaporated, and they sit out a social engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: SELFCONCEIT minus S, E, E leaves LFCONCIT, which 'dispelled' rearranges; 'see out' says those three letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: A military engagement is a battle or clash, a fight between opposing sides.

clue.text: Source regularly mined?

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the word Source, starting with its second

explanation.surface: A question about a supply that is dug out on a routine basis.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth and sixth letters of 'Source' are taken; the whole clue then describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal-bearing rock is the raw material dug from a mine, the source of iron or copper.

clue.text: Fellow 'sampling' every second? Bloody odd TV chef

indicators.note: sampling suggests taking only some of the letters of the phrase that follows
every second picks the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of Bloody odd

explanation.surface: A man sampling dishes constantly, an oddball television cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Keith Floyd was a British TV cook, famous for cooking with a glass of wine in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Floyd presented popular cookery programmes on British television from the 1980s onwards, an example of a TV chef.

clue.text: Setter's in favour of half-hearted waffle? Unlikely

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so setter's = I'm, I am
pro means in favour of

indicators.note: half-hearted removes half of the heart, one of the two middle letters of the word for waffle

parts.note: to babble is to waffle, talk on pointlessly

explanation.surface: The compiler supports some feeble waffling, which seems unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: BABBLE has BB at its heart; 'half-hearted' drops one B to give BABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something not expected to happen, direct synonyms.

clue.text: 'Revolver' artist

definitions.meaning: literally one who revolves or rotates something
J. M. W. ..., the English landscape painter

explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around 'Revolver' signal the playful literal reading, not the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a person or thing that spins; the other is the English Romantic painter J.M.W. Turner.

clue.text: Mediterranean island country once 25% smaller

indicators.note: smaller means the former country's name is cut down by losing some letters

parts.note: Rhodesia is the former name of Zimbabwe
a quarter of the eight-letter former country is two letters, its final pair

explanation.surface: A Mediterranean island compared to a former country that has shrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: RHODESIA has eight letters; cutting 25% means losing two, the IA at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea, the largest of the Dodecanese group.

clue.text: Herb gathered for basic sauce

indicators.note: gathered here means understood by ear, as in 'I gather', so the herb's name is heard

parts.note: rue is a bitter aromatic herb

explanation.surface: Herbs are picked to make a simple sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathered' looks like picking herbs, but means what one hears.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooked mixture of flour and fat is the base from which white sauces such as béchamel are built.

clue.text: Past master avoiding pressure to work too hard

parts.note: over means past or finished

indicators.note: avoiding means the word for master does without the letter for pressure

parts.note: an expert is a master of a skill
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A former expert who takes it easy rather than working too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: EXPERT without P gives EXERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To push oneself beyond reasonable limits is to strain excessively, labouring beyond what is healthy.

clue.text: Internet era's transformed role of host?

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The internet age has changed what it means to be a host.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'era' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A host at a party or on a show amuses the guests or audience, so the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: Indemnify soldiers before palace revolution

indicators.note: before places the soldiers ahead of the uprising

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers
a coup is a seizure of power from within, a palace revolution

explanation.surface: Troops are compensated ahead of an overthrow at court.
explanation.definitionFit: To indemnify is to compensate for a loss, much as one makes good or reimburses money spent.

clue.text: Way to cover rent? Wheel of Fortune, possibly

indicators.note: to cover means the word for way wraps around the word for rent

parts.note: a route is a way to get somewhere
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a way to pay the rent, maybe on a TV game show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheel of Fortune' looks like the game show; here it is a casino wheel, so 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino game with a spinning numbered wheel is a fortune wheel in the most literal sense of gambling.

clue.text: Briefly scrutinise one disturbing Ashes game

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to study is to scrutinise closely
a poker is a rod used to stir the ashes and embers of a fire

explanation.surface: A quick look at a player who unsettles an Ashes cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the England v Australia Test cricket series, but here it is just fireplace ash.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker variant where some cards are dealt face up is a card game for gamblers.

clue.text: Worldly queen joining others in competition

indicators.note: in puts the queen and others inside the word for competition

parts.note: a trial is a test or competition, as in sheepdog trials
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a standard crossword queen
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: An earthly monarch joins the rest in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Of this world, earthly rather than heavenly: the sense of belonging to the Earth.

clue.text: Fruit plant being delivered

indicators.note: delivered as in a speech delivered, so the word is spoken

parts.note: to plant something is to bury it in the soil

explanation.surface: A fruiting plant arrives by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a noun beside 'Fruit'; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A small juicy fruit such as a raspberry or strawberry, picked from a bush.

clue.text: Out of favour in graduate party, gloomy

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
a do is a party
dour means gloomy or stern

explanation.surface: A sombre graduate at a party who has fallen from favour.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being disliked or in disgrace, as though one carried a bad smell.

clue.text: Old Macdonald perhaps going after sheep

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
say means perhaps, for example

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme farmer chasing his flock.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramsay MacDonald was the first Labour Prime Minister, not the farmer of the nursery rhyme; 'going after' places the second piece behind the sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsay MacDonald led Britain's first Labour government in 1924, a long-dead politician.

clue.text: Fun time supporting Robin Hood's band reportedly

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the time letter goes last
reportedly means as said aloud, so the band's name is heard

parts.note: Robin Hood's outlaw band were the Merry Men

explanation.surface: An enjoyable spell spent backing Robin Hood's outlaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean jollity, cheerful enjoyment and laughter.

clue.text: Guts are key at the outset

parts.note: Enter is a key on a computer keyboard, and at the outset puts it first
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Courage is essential from the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' and 'are' read as courage being key; 'are' is the metric unit of 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of enteron, the alimentary canal, so a medical word for intestines.

clue.text: Records what's essentially sent from pulsar

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, so the middle letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Data is logged from signals sent by a pulsing star.
explanation.definitionFit: To record a name on a list is to sign it up or register it.

clue.text: Bird hurting both wings flying

indicators.note: the wings are the end letters of the word for hurting; flying means they leave

parts.note: smarting means stinging or hurting

explanation.surface: A bird in pain because both its wings were hurt in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' and 'wings flying' look like one picture; the wings are the outer letters S and G.
explanation.definitionFit: The house martin and sand martin are small swallow-like birds.

clue.text: Ex-chancellor attached to following rules

indicators.note: following places the word for attached after the rules

parts.note: laws are rules
on means attached to, as in a lid on a jar

explanation.surface: A former finance minister stuck to the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Lawson was Chancellor of the Exchequer, the UK finance minister, from 1983 to 1989.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Lawson served as Margaret Thatcher's Chancellor of the Exchequer, the British finance minister.

clue.text: This is returned, empty, by one at Oktoberfest

definitions.text: This is returned, empty, by one at Oktoberfest

indicators.note: returned means the two outer letters are read backwards
empty means the word This is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: ein is German for one, and Oktoberfest is the Munich beer festival

explanation.surface: A beer drinker in Munich hands back an empty mug.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the large mug that a reveller hands back once drained.
explanation.definitionFit: A large beer mug, typically earthenware, used for beer in Germany, hence drained and handed back at a beer festival.

clue.text: Revellers and roués drunkenly crashing cars

indicators.note: crashing means barging into, so the rearranged letters go inside cars
drunkenly suggests reeling about, so the letters of roués are rearranged

explanation.surface: Partygoers and rakes crash their cars while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' gives OUSER, which 'crashing' puts inside the vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: People who drink and make merry noisily at a party are a direct synonym for partygoers.

clue.text: Specialist making iron tools and horseshoes principally

definitions.text: Specialist making iron tools and horseshoes principally

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so the first letters of the five words are taken

explanation.surface: A description of the craftsman at the forge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' is skipped; the initials of the other five words spell the answer, and the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith or farrier forges metal tools and shoes horses, a metalworking craftsman.

clue.text: Superior abstainer quits this?

indicators.note: quits means the abstainer leaves the word for superior

parts.note: better means superior
TT, teetotal, means an abstainer from alcohol

explanation.surface: A virtuous teetotaller gives up drinking, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the drink an abstainer gives up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale or lager is an alcoholic drink, exactly what a teetotaller renounces.

clue.text: Everlasting night when this is nigh?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: take the word night with the T for time removed and it becomes nigh

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about when darkness draws close.
explanation.walkthrough: T is time; 'night' minus T gives 'nigh', so the answer, split in two, is the instruction that turns one into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unaffected by time lasts for ever, so a synonym for eternal.

clue.text: Reed organ backing core of choir

indicators.note: backing means the organ supports from behind, coming after the core letter
core of means the central letter of choir

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A reed organ accompanying the heart of a church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reed organ' looks like an instrument; Reed is the actor Oliver Reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Reed was the English film actor, so his forename partners the surname given.

clue.text: Animal in tree escaping from trap

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, so words escaping from it are spoken

parts.note: the yew is an evergreen tree

explanation.surface: A creature up a tree gets free of a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' looks like a snare; it is slang for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is an example of a farm animal.

clue.text: Worker up on ridge — maybe he'll run down

definitions.meaning: a roofer who lays stone tiles works up on the roof ridge
to slate is to criticise harshly, so one who does this runs others down

explanation.walkthrough: The roofer might also come down the ladder; the second sense is a critic.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer laying stone tiles, and also one who criticises harshly, as in slating a play.

clue.text: Viking found here breaking no hearts

indicators.note: breaking means smashing apart, so the letters of no hearts are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Norse raider who comes ashore without breaking hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: Viking is a sea area in the BBC Shipping Forecast, not a Norse warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Viking is one of the Shipping Forecast's named sea areas, lying in the northern part of that stretch of water between Britain and Norway.
